headline: Growing from ~$500K ARR to $9.5M ARR within 24 months as major contract rollout begins; Mexican bank trial and NZ bank renewal demonstrate pipeline beyond single-customer concentration
reasoning: RocketBoots has a major contracted transformation deal worth over $9 million per year on a five-year term, signed approximately December of the prior year. The company is at an inflection point, transitioning from roughly $500,000 ARR today to over $9.5 million ARR within 24 months as the rollout of their technology begins. A trial with a major Mexican retail bank (1,200+ branches) is underway with a multinational consulting partner with whom they have a pre-negotiated reseller agreement, reducing competitive risk. A New Zealand bank 12-month renewal extends what will be a four-year enterprise relationship. No capital raise is currently planned, though concentration risk in a single major customer is acknowledged. The CEO argues market discount reflects execution wait-and-see but upcoming months will demonstrate contract delivery.
quote: We look at the contracted value. I mean, I understand that the market would discount us at this point, you know that they're waiting for execution of the contract, which you know over the coming months they're going to be able to start witnessing the the, the execution of that contract. Now the current timeline for that contract sees us going from basically $500,000 of ARR today to over $9.5 million of ARR in 24 months once the rollout of our technology begins. And we're at the basically at the starting line now and that role that is about to start.
episode_title: RocketBoots puts the pedal to the metal

headline: Emphasising long-term recurring revenue model with enterprise contracts now reaching Year 4 with a New Zealand bank customer
reasoning: Joel Rappolt highlighted that RocketBoots focuses on recurring licence revenue rather than one-off project revenue. A New Zealand bank customer first engaged in 2009, paused during COVID, and re-engaged afterwards; the current enterprise contract renewal will take the relationship to four years. Rappolt expressed confidence the customer would not move away and noted the announcement was intended to demonstrate the durability of long-term customer relationships.
quote: No, no, the it's a rolling a new renewal as it said in the announcement like this, this customer first engaged with us in 2009 pre COVID. We had a pretty successful initial run with them. Everything slowed down during COVID and after COVID we re engaged. But you know, I mean this is the, since the enterprise contract was signed, this is this is, this will take us up to a full four years. I mean, I don't see any reason why they would move away from our service. But yeah, it's four years today. Look again, the reason that we we wanted to release that is again we're about recurring revenue, long term recurring recurring revenue. We're not just once off project revenue, it's, you know, over a long period of time we get to licence our software to our customers. And today's announcement was just to demonstrate again for another customer, you know, we're getting up to Year 4.
episode_title: RocketBoots puts the pedal to the metal
